newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 2.8 pct to fresh record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 2.8 pct to fresh record.

text.p: Istanbul stock market index rose sharply to a new record close amid selective buying on Wednesday, following Tuesday's 2.16 percent downward correction to the medium-term uptrend, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at an all-time high of 83,772.33, up 2,267.92 points, or 2.78 percent from Tuesday and compared to Monday's previous high of 83,300.95.
Daily trade volume rose to 19.66 trillion lira ($206.3 million) from Tuesday's 17.30 trillion ($181.5 million).
"Selective activity enlivened again in the afternoon after rather narrow trade (range) in the morning," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti investment bank.

Many brokers expect selective demand based on nine-month profit prospects to be firm on Thursday and Friday because settlements of transactions will be delayed to next Wednesday and Thursday, respectively due to an official holiday next week.
Turkish markets will be closed Monday afternoon and Tuesday due to Republic Day. Deals done on Monday morning will also be settled next Thursday.
The index has surged 29.3 percent since September 13, breaking ten record closes in the strong medium-term uptrend which began with the breaching of 65,000 barrier.
